harness_bug_found_and_fixed.symptom: SIGTERM appeared to have no effect: no '[engine] caught signal' line, no shutdown sequence, process exited near-instantly with no teardown breakpoints firing
harness_bug_found_and_fixed.root_cause: the driver captured $! after `timeout ... gdb ... &`, which is timeout's PID, not gdb's; `pgrep -P` on that PID returned gdb itself, so kill -TERM was sent to gdb (killing the whole ptraced tree) instead of to the fluent-bit inferior
harness_bug_found_and_fixed.diagnosis: a plain (non-gdb) SIGTERM control run showed normal ~50ms graceful shutdown with full teardown logging; a minimal gdb script breaking only on flb_sched_destroy/flb_config_exit confirmed those breakpoints fire once the PID resolution is corrected
harness_bug_found_and_fixed.fix: resolve gdb's real PID as the child of the timeout PID, then the inferior's PID as the child of gdb's PID, before sending SIGTERM
harness_bug_found_and_fixed.scope: this is a bug in this card's own run harness, not in any script from the run guide; all candidate runs recorded below post-date the fix

FB-SINGLEPLEX-RETRY-FLUSH-FAULT.fault_point: src/flb_output.c:330 (flb_output_task_flush call in flb_output_task_queue_flush_one, after the temporary user was dropped at :329)
FB-SINGLEPLEX-RETRY-FLUSH-FAULT.mechanism: breakpoint at flb_output_task_flush's entry, conditioned on the queued task's pointer, forces `return -1` at entry for the fault run only, simulating a flush-creation/pipe-write failure

script_fix.guide_text: type `step` to enter flb_output_task_flush, then `return -1`, answer y, then `continue`
script_fix.problem: the call at flb_output.c:330-332 spans multiple source lines for argument evaluation; a single `step` from the line-330 breakpoint only advances within that same call's argument lines rather than entering the callee, so `return -1` would pop the wrong frame
script_fix.evidence_of_failure: runs/c3-fault-attempt1-discarded.log (stalled at the intermediate source line, SIGTERM sent but no clean resume)
script_fix.fix: added a second breakpoint directly at the entry of flb_output_task_flush, conditioned on the queued task's pointer, and issued `return -1` there instead

FB-SINGLEPLEX-RETRY-FLUSH-FAULT.queueing_setup: with the output forced synchronous, flb_output_task_flush's non-threaded arm is asynchronous by construction (writes an out_flush pointer through config->ch_self_events and returns 0 immediately; the callback runs on a later event-loop tick), so a second task's scheduled retry naturally lands in the singleplex queue's pending list behind the one still in-progress -- no extra input or raised rate was needed
